answer: Fund shared goods with pairwise-bounded quadratic matching. Plain quadratic funding rewards headcount, so a grove of sybil wallets each giving one coin could drain the matching oasis. Instead, every pair of donors' joint subsidy term is capped by M/(M+k), where k counts other projects both have backed. Clones moving in lockstep share a huge k, so their pairwise terms collapse toward zero, while strangers who rarely overlap keep full matching. Splitting one budget across many keys climbs no ridge of extra subsidy.
